symptom: On a project with a source index, every catalog rebuild — `refresh catalog`, and the implicit ones `search` / `show references` start after any save — described every document again: 38 s on a 4,753-unit app on macOS, hours on Windows before ako/mxcli#1789, repeated after every edit in an agent loop
cause: By design a refresh rebuilds at least the cached level (#1081, `cmd_catalog.go`), and `buildSource` had no memory of what it had described before, so the cheapest rebuild that could still be saved was the most expensive one
insight: **A row is reusable only if everything its describe read is unchanged, and the describe reads more than its own unit.** Three dependencies turned up, each found by a step of the equality test (incremental vs forced full build, row for row, after each kind of edit): other documents named in the refs (a page prints its data-source flow's return entity: `-- Context: $currentObject (M.ProbeA)`); the unit's container, which is a Unit-table column and not in the bytes, so a move into an existing folder kept the stale `folder` line; and the describer itself (fingerprint = executable path, size, mtime). **The equality test needs a control that breaks the dependency logic**: with `sourceDependents` stubbed to return nothing the first version of the test still passed, because none of its edits changed a dependent's text; the page-context step is what made it fail. Anything the plan cannot follow (a changed unit that is not a described document: folder, module, settings, Java action) falls back to describing everything, so reuse is an optimisation of the full build and never a different answer. FactoryManagement: one attribute added, plain refresh 11.2 s vs 38.2 s, 3,525 of 3,718 rows reused, byte-identical to `force`
